ANOVA Tables for lmer Fits with Kenward-Roger or Satterthwaite df

Source: R/anova.R
anova.lmerMod.Rd

anova() of a single lmer fit (and of a gaussian semireg fit, fit$semer) gives F tests with denominator degrees of freedom, computed by the package's own code: Type III tests with Kenward-Roger df by default, as SAS PROC MIXED DDFM=KR. This replaces the tables of lmerTest, which predictmeans attached before 2.0. With several models, anova(m1, m2) is lme4's likelihood ratio comparison, unchanged.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'lmerMod'
anova(
  object,
  ...,
  type = c("III", "II", "I"),
  ddf = c("Kenward-Roger", "Satterthwaite", "lme4"),
  advice = TRUE
)

Arguments

object

An lmer fit (class lmerMod).

...

Other fitted models: then lme4's comparison of the models.

type

"III" (default), "II" or "I"; also 3, 2, 1.

ddf

"Kenward-Roger" (default), "Satterthwaite" or "lme4".

advice

Logical: add a note on the choice of type when the data are unbalanced or have empty cells (default TRUE).

Value

An anova table: for each term the numerator df, the denominator df (column heading names the method), the F value and its p-value. With advice = TRUE a note on the type is kept in attr(, "advice") (read it with advice).

Details

Type III hypotheses do not depend on the contrasts the model was fitted with (sum-to-zero coding, as SAS Type 3). With empty cells (aliased coefficients) each term is tested on the cells with data: an interaction by its contrasts that use no empty cell (one df fewer per empty cell), a main effect whose means average over empty cells on the cells its means share, as pm_joint; the table says so, and the intercept is not tested; Type II are those of car::Anova(); Type I (sequential) are lmerTest's, always with Satterthwaite df. Kenward-Roger F tests use the adjusted covariance of the fixed effects (pbkrtest's, observed information); a variance component estimated as zero is left out of the adjustment, as in SAS. ddf = "lme4" gives lme4's own table (sums of squares and F values without df or p-values).

With lmerTest attached, lmer() is lmerTest's and its fits are of class lmerModLmerTest: their anova() and summary() are lmerTest's (Satterthwaite by default), and this method applies to fits of lme4::lmer(). Everything else in predictmeans works the same with either class.

Which type of test

With balanced data (equal numbers in all cells) Types I, II and III give the same tests. With unbalanced data:

Type I

sequential: each term adjusted for the terms before it, so the order in the formula matters. Use it when the order is meaningful, e.g. a block or a covariate to be removed first.

Type II

each term adjusted for all terms that do not contain it (the principle of marginality). The most powerful tests of main effects when the interactions are negligible; with an interaction present the main effects are not well defined.

Type III

each term adjusted for all others, testing equally weighted cell means; meaningful with an interaction present, and here independent of the model's contrasts. A covariate in an interaction makes the other terms be tested at covariate = 0: centre it.

With empty cells no type answers the question of a main effect over all cells: Type III uses the cells with data (and says so). State the comparisons of interest on the cell means instead, with pm_joint or predictmeans.

See also

anova.semireg, pm_joint, df_term, permmodels

Examples

library(predictmeans)
Oats$nitro <- factor(Oats$nitro)
fm <- lmer(yield ~ nitro*Variety + (1|Block/Variety), data = Oats)
anova(fm)
#> Analysis of Deviance Table (Type III Wald F tests with Kenward-Roger df)
#> 
#> Response: yield
#>                      F Df Df.res    Pr(>F)    
#> (Intercept)   245.1374  1      5 1.932e-05 ***
#> nitro          37.6857  3     45 2.458e-12 ***
#> Variety         1.4853  2     10    0.2724    
#> nitro:Variety   0.3028  6     45    0.9322    
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
anova(fm, ddf = "Satterthwaite")
#> Analysis of Deviance Table (Type III Wald F tests with Satterthwaite df)
#> 
#> Response: yield
#>                      F Df Df.res    Pr(>F)    
#> (Intercept)   245.1374  1      5 1.932e-05 ***
#> nitro          37.6857  3     45 2.458e-12 ***
#> Variety         1.4853  2     10    0.2724    
#> nitro:Variety   0.3028  6     45    0.9322    
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
anova(fm, type = "I")
#> Type I Analysis of Variance Table with Satterthwaite's method
#>                Sum Sq Mean Sq NumDF DenDF F value    Pr(>F)    
#> nitro         20020.5  6673.5     3    45 37.6857 2.458e-12 ***
#> Variety         526.1   263.0     2    10  1.4853    0.2724    
#> nitro:Variety   321.7    53.6     6    45  0.3028    0.9322    
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
